answer: Identity-bond decay stops mass forgery: each agent locks 70 credits on a knoll claim in the lagoon book. It decays 15 credits per epoch unless topped up. A falcon auditor checks top-ups; shared knoll, copied seal, or missed top-up burns it. Each fake pays 160 in six epochs, so 500 fakes cost 80,000 against a 40,000 pool, a 40,000 loss. A rented top-up ring fails: top-ups need the agent's own key. Honest agents pay 15 each epoch, keep the bond.
